Mar 2026 and Sep 2026 company materials show topline now guided to 1H 2027, with no results public. Borderline: a vague 'favorable' interim statement exists, but it is a sample-size/continuation decision, not a primary result.

quote: Across both studies, at target doses, sevasemten was well-tolerated.
notes: Registered primary outcomes are adverse events. The release gives a vague, combined (LYNX and FOX) tolerability statement plus unquantified early FOX efficacy comments. Weak and borderline; flag for review.

Cited release (2026-01-09) only moves the PIVOT-006 topline timing to 1H 2026. The Q2 2026 release (2026-08-06) still says results are coming 'soon' with the vast majority of target events accrued. I found no topline result or stop; a later release may exist that I could not find.

2025-01-22 interim release (68 patients) says JK07 was safe and well tolerated, with 'trends towards improvement' in early efficacy, but does not clearly address the registered primary (LVEF, week 26). The Sep 2025 release guided the primary analysis to 1H 2026, and I found no topline. Judgement call.

The 2026-10-12 data are from the open-label portion (25 participants), presented at ISFTD (NfL, GFAP, tolerability). They are not the randomized comparison; the full randomized results are guided to Q1 2027.

The 2026-05-11 release covers completion of Part A, with 'no safety concerns identified' and a Safety Review Committee endorsing progression to Part B. This is a lead-in safety part. Registered primaries are only Part A safety, so this is borderline; no Part B efficacy result or stop was found.
